source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Check if the appliance is labeled with a model or serial number.
3. Inspect and check the appliance for visible damage.
4. Document the type of check performed, e.g., PAT (Portable Appliance Testing).
5. Record the date and time of the test.
6. Identify any observed visual defects (e.g., frayed cords, cracked housing).
7. Write down whether the plug is correctly wired.
8. If any signs of overheating are present, make a note of them.
9. Describe the state of the fuse, and whether it is the correct rating.
10. Detail any issues with the continuity of the earth bond.
11. Measure and record the insulation resistance readings.
12. Record any earth leakage current results.
13. List all lodged defects and concerns that need rectification.
14. Attach before-repair images, if applicable.
15. State whether the appliance has failed or passed the safety check.
16. Note any
